title: Anti-NMDAR Encephalitis and Pediatric Autoimmune Encephalitis
subject: ss-paediatric-neurology

steps.say: Anti NMDAR encephalitis represents the commonest autoimmune encephalitis in children, frequently presenting with behavioural disturbance.
steps.tx: Evaluate **Anti-NMDAR epidemiology in children** when investigating subacute neuropsychiatric deterioration. Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis is recognized as the most frequent autoimmune encephalitis in the pediatric population, accounting for more than 40-50% of all antibody-mediated pediatric encephalitides. Unlike older patients, young children under twelve years of age often present with non-psychotic behavioural changes such as severe temper tantrums, hyperactivity, aggression, insomnia, and speech regression rather than formal auditory or visual hallucinations (Multi-stage clinical progression).

vis.alt: Teratoma driven antibodies internalising synaptic NMDA receptors in hippocampus.
vis.caption: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis: antibodies remove synaptic receptors. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The multi-stage clinical progression moves from a viral prodrome to psychiatric symptoms, seizures, and movement disorders.
steps.tx: Trace the **Multi-stage clinical progression** characteristic of anti-NMDAR encephalitis in children. The illness typically unfolds in distinct phases: beginning with a nonspecific prodromal viral-like illness (low-grade fever, malaise, headache); progressing within two weeks to severe neuropsychiatric disturbance and insomnia; followed by rapid speech breakdown, cognitive regression, and intractable seizures; and culminating in an advanced movement disorder stage with profound catatonia, hypoventilation, and autonomic instability (Orofacial dyskinesias).

vis.alt: Antibody mediated neuronal attack with paraneoplastic triggers and imaging findings.
vis.caption: Autoimmune encephalitis: antibodies attack neuronal targets. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Orofacial dyskinesias represent pathognomonic movement disorders in children with anti NMDAR encephalitis.
steps.tx: Recognise stereotypic **Orofacial dyskinesias** as pathognomonic hyperkinetic movement disorders in pediatric anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Affected children manifest continuous, involuntary movements including rhythmic lip-smacking, tongue-thrusting, chewing, and forceful jaw-chomping, which frequently causes severe self-inflicted mucosal ulcerations and tongue lacerations. These orofacial automatisms are frequently accompanied by choreoathetosis, dystonic posturing of the limbs, oculogyric crises, and sudden catatonic stupor (Extreme delta brush EEG pattern).

rows: Provide soft mouthguards and sedation to prevent self-mutilation
Extraocular muscles with sustained upward gaze
Differentiate from focal epileptic seizures via continuous EEG

steps.say: The extreme delta brush EEG pattern shows rhythmic delta activity with superimposed fast beta runs in nearly a third of patients.
steps.tx: Identify the **Extreme delta brush EEG pattern** as an electrophysiological hallmark in anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Present in approximately 30% of hospitalized patients, this unique waveform features continuous, rhythmic 1-3 Hz delta slow waves with superimposed bursts of fast 20-30 Hz beta activity riding on each delta wave crest. Its appearance closely resembles the physiological delta brush of premature neonates, correlates strongly with prolonged hospitalization, and serves as an electroencephalographic signature of NMDA receptor hypofunction (Ovarian teratoma age relationship).

rows: Reflects profound frontotemporal and subcortical encephalopathy
Rides on the troughs and peaks of slow delta rhythms
Associated with prolonged intensive care admission and coma

steps.say: The ovarian teratoma age relationship shows a low frequency in young girls compared to adult women.
steps.tx: Consider the **Ovarian teratoma age relationship** when ordering oncologic investigations in pediatric females. While adult females display an underlying ovarian teratoma in more than 50% of cases, prepubertal pediatric girls (< 12 years) have a markedly low teratoma frequency of under 10%. Despite this low incidence, pelvic ultrasonography or non-contrast pelvic MRI remains an essential baseline screening investigation in all post-pubertal adolescent females to exclude occult paraneoplastic teratomas driving the autoimmune response (First-line immunotherapy triple regimen).

left.title: Pediatric Girls (< 12 years)
points: Ovarian teratoma found in < 10% of cases
Pathology is predominantly post-infectious or idiopathic autoimmunity
Repeat imaging only if clinical relapse occurs

right.title: Adolescent & Adult Females
points: Ovarian teratoma present in > 50% of adult women
Tumour contains neural tissue expressing GluN1 subunits
Screening: mandatory high-resolution pelvic MRI / CT
Prompt surgical oophorectomy or cystectomy is curative

steps.say: First line immunotherapy triple regimen combines pulse steroids with immunoglobulin and plasma exchange.
steps.tx: Initiate the **First-line immunotherapy triple regimen** promptly upon clinical diagnosis without awaiting antibody results. The standard first-line protocol comprises high-dose intravenous pulse methylprednisolone administered at 30 mg/kg/day (maximum 1000 mg/day) for 5 days, combined with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) dosed at 2 g/kg divided over 2-5 days. In severe or rapidly worsening cases with profound encephalopathy, therapeutic plasma exchange (PLEX, 5-7 cycles) is deployed to rapidly remove circulating anti-GluN1 antibodies (Second-line escalation with rituximab).

nodes.label: Co-administer IVIG (2 g/kg) or PLEX (5-7 cycles)

steps.say: Second line escalation with rituximab or cyclophosphamide is required when first line therapy fails after ten to fourteen days.
steps.tx: Execute **Second-line escalation with rituximab** or intravenous cyclophosphamide if objective neurological improvement is absent after 10-14 days of first-line immunotherapy. Rituximab is dosed at 375 mg/m2 intravenous infusion weekly for 4 doses to eliminate CD20+ B cells and arrest pathogenic plasmablast differentiation. In severe refractory cases or when rituximab is unavailable, intravenous pulse cyclophosphamide (500-750 mg/m2 monthly) is added, significantly reducing long-term relapse and accelerating cognitive recovery (Post-HSV encephalitis autoimmune trigger).

left.title: First-Line Response Assessment
points: Evaluate clinical status at 10-14 days of steroid/IVIG therapy
Approximately 50% of pediatric patients achieve substantial recovery
If encephalopathy, seizures, or dyskinesias persist, escalate promptly

right.title: Second-Line Regimen
points: Rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV weekly for 4 doses (depletes CD20+ B cells)
Intravenous cyclophosphamide in severe refractory encephalitis
Dramatically reduces disease relapse and improves functional outcomes

steps.say: A post HSV encephalitis autoimmune trigger causes chorea relapse weeks after negative viral PCR.
steps.tx: Recognise the **Post-HSV encephalitis autoimmune trigger** in children recovering from herpes simplex virus (HSV-1) encephalitis. Approximately 25% of pediatric HSV encephalitis patients experience secondary neurological deterioration 2 to 8 weeks following initial treatment. The presentation features acute chorea, cognitive decline, and insomnia despite repeat CSF HSV PCR testing remaining negative. Viral-induced neuronal cytolysis releases GluN1 synaptic antigens that prime secondary anti-NMDAR autoimmunity, mandating prompt immunotherapy rather than reinstituting acyclovir.

nodes.label: Neuronal lysis releases synaptic antigens (2 to 8 weeks)
Develops in ~25% of pediatric cases: chorea & agitation
Negative repeat HSV PCR -> Prompt IVIG & steroids
